Title: On Meeks' conjecture on disjoint minimal graphs
Authors: Angelo Benedetti, Barbara Nelli
Date: Wed Oct 14 17:12:50 2026

We study disjoint solution pairs $(u,D)$ to the minimal surface equation in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $u=0$ on $\partial D.$ A conjecture of W. Meeks states that at most two such pairs can exist in $\mathbb{R}^n.$ We confirm the conjecture in two complementary cases. For $n\in\{2,3,4,5,6\},$ we prove it under a superlinearity assumption. In dimension $n=2,$ we establish the result under a suitable sublinearity assumption. We also derive estimates on the asymptotic angle of domains supporting nontrivial solutions for $n\geq 3.$--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# TWO-DIMENSIONAL DISJOINT MINIMAL GRAPHS

LINFENG ZHOU

Under the assumption of Gauss curvature vanishing at infinity, we prove Meeks’ conjecture: the number of disjointly supported minimal graphs in ℝ³ is at most two.

## 1. Introduction

Let Ω be an open subset in ℝ² and denote its boundary by ∂Ω. As we know, if a function u(x) defined on Ω satisfies the equation

(1)  div \(\dfrac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\) = 0,

\(G = \{(x, u(x)) : x \in \Omega\}\) is called a minimal graph in ℝ³. We say the minimal graph G is supported on Ω if \(u|_{\partial \Omega} = 0\) and \(u \ge 0\).

Meeks [2005] has conjectured that the number of disjointly supported minimal graphs with zero boundary values over an open subset in ℝ² is at most 2. In fact, for arbitrary dimension, Meeks and Rosenberg [2005] proved if a set of disjointly supported minimal graphs have bounded gradient, then the number of the graphs must be finite. Later, Li and Wang [2001] gave an upper bound of the number of the graphs without any assumption on the growth rate of each graph. As a corollary, when minimal graphs are two dimensional in ℝ³, they obtained the number is at most 24. At the same time, Spruck [2002] proved that there are at most two admissible sublinear growth solution pairs of Equation (1) defined over disjoint domains. Recently, by using angular density, Tkachev [2009] showed the number of two dimensional disjointly supported minimal graphs is less than or equals 3.

Abstract:

We provide an estimate of the amenable category of oriented closed connected complete affine manifolds whose fundamental group contains an infinite amenable normal subgroup. As an application we show that all such manifolds have zero simplicial volume. This answers a question by L\"uck in the case of complete affine manifolds. Our construction also provides the vanishing of stable integral simplicial volume and minimal volume entropy. This means that such manifolds satisfy integral approximation.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What happened

A linear map between C*-algebras is a spectral isometry if it preserves the spectral radius of every element. Kadison showed long ago that maps preserving the norm are Jordan *-isomorphisms. Mathieu and Schick conjectured in 2002 that spectral isometries are Jordan isomorphisms too. This was known for commutative algebras and other special classes.

On 29 Oct Matthew Colbrook and George Stepaniants posted a proof for all unital C*-algebras. They describe the paper as a human digest of a proof GPT-6 Astra found “after a sequence of simple prompts”. They say they studied the argument with ChatGPT 6 and then wrote the paper themselves. A Lean proof was registered on Palomar the day before.

## Why it matters

The conjecture is a standard open problem on spectrum-preserving maps, listed in Mathieu’s 2009 problem collection. With a Lean proof and named authors at Cambridge, it is one of the better-documented AI results of October. It follows the same “AI proof, human digest” format as Colbrook’s Smale paper.
